title: German Firms Eye Hyderabad as Innovation Base as Indo-German Ties Hit New High
excerpt: Consul General Michael Hasper says German companies are setting up global capability centres in Hyderabad, bilateral trade stands near $50 billion, and 70,000 Indian students now study in Germany.
body:
• German companies are looking at Hyderabad as a base for innovation, research and technology development, Consul General Michael Hasper said at a Day of German Unity reception in Hyderabad on October 30.
  • Hasper put bilateral trade in goods and services at around $50 billion; Germany is India's largest trading partner in the European Union and one of its leading investors.
  • Around 70,000 Indian students now study at German universities — Germany's largest international student community — and about 350,000 Indians live in Germany, the largest Indian community in continental Europe.
  • India and Germany are marking 75 years of diplomatic relations and 25 years of strategic partnership, and Hasper said the upcoming EU-India free trade agreement will open further opportunities.

German companies are looking at Hyderabad as a base for innovation, research and tech development, the German Consul General in Chennai, Michael Hasper, said on Friday, describing Indo-German relations as thriving. "Germany and India have never been as close as they are today, politically, economically, and between our societies, and all of that is very much happening here in Telangana and also in Hyderabad," Hasper told ANI on the sidelines of a Day of German Unity reception hosted by the consulate at The Park hotel in Hyderabad, as reported by Devdiscourse.

"Many German companies come here to set up their Global Capability Centres. We will see a lot of Indo-German economic ties being built in the years to come."

— Michael Hasper, German Consul General, Chennai

The numbers behind the claim

Hasper said bilateral trade in goods and services stands at around $50 billion, with Germany India's largest trading partner in the European Union and one of its leading investors. He pointed to the upcoming EU-India Free Trade Agreement as a further opening for industrial, technological and commercial cooperation. The two countries are marking 75 years of diplomatic relations and 25 years of their strategic partnership.

https://x.com/ANI/status/2116187900660601083

Talent runs in both directions

The people flow is as significant as the trade. Around 70,000 Indian students now study at German universities — the largest international student community in the country — and around 350,000 Indians live in Germany, making it the largest Indian community in continental Europe, Hasper said. "For young people from Telangana, Germany offers an excellent education, exciting research, and great career opportunities. At the same time, Germany needs skilled professionals: engineers, IT specialists, technicians, and healthcare workers. Telangana has an abundance of talent," he said. "Connecting that talent with opportunities in Germany makes perfect sense for both sides."

Why Hyderabad

For Hyderabad, the GCC flow is the concrete prize: each German capability centre brings engineering and research jobs that would previously have defaulted to Bengaluru, and state officials have courted German investors across life sciences, automotive and advanced manufacturing. The Hindu's report of Hasper's remarks, which the selector flagged for this story, is here. The test of Hasper's optimism will be whether announced interest converts into named centres and hiring over the next year.
